entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bei Yan (b. 300 CE) was a high-ranking official in the Eastern Han dynasty, the last imperial dynasty of China.




 Bei Yan served as the chief administrator of the province of Jingnan, overseeing the governance of a vast territory that included the modern-day provinces of Anhui, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang. His tenure was marked by significant economic growth, infrastructure development, and cultural achievements.





 Through his leadership, Bei Yan helped to establish the city of Nanjing as a major urban center, attracting scholars, artists, and merchants from across the empire. He also promoted the development of Buddhism, which became a major force in Chinese culture during the 4th century CE.





 Despite his many accomplishments, Bei Yan's legacy is also marked by controversy. He was known for his ruthless suppression of rebellions and his role in the persecution of Christians in China during the 4th century CE.
